primitives.name: Short-arm throw kinematics
primitives.verbatim_quote: 208 WALTER CAMP'S BOOK OF COLLEGE SPORTS and feeble, but constant practice speedily results in moderate speed and peculiar accuracy.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'k_{\\text{practice}}': 'Dimensionless practice efficiency coefficient', 't': 'Time since start of practice [s]', '\\alpha': 'Exponent describing acceleration rate (0 < \\alpha < 1)'}
primitives.assumptions: Power-law skill acquisition with diminishing returns; linear relationship between practice duration and achievable velocity; constant environmental conditions.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Non-negativity constraints: v(t) \geq 0, t \geq 0; singularity at t=0 requiring initial condition v(0)=0.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI sequential probability ratio test for detecting anomalous throws; maps to GSE state-transition model for evaluating catcher positioning.
layer2.telemetry: Observed throw velocity distribution P(v|t) compared against baseline power-law model.

primitives.name: Forward-motion throw constraint
primitives.verbatim_quote: The secret of the throw is, of course, keeping the hand in a line with the arm and not swinging it out to the side and away from the head, where much of the accuracy and some of the quickness is lost.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'{\\bf r}(t)': 'Position vector from shoulder to release point [m]', '{\\bf v}(t)': 'Velocity vector at release [m/s]'}
primitives.assumptions: Collinear hand-arm configuration minimizes lateral deviation; optimal alignment maximizes momentum transfer along the intended trajectory.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Perfect collinearity ({\bf r} \parallel {\bf v}) yields maximum efficiency; any angular deviation introduces energy loss via perpendicular components.

layer2.mapping: Bayesian conformal prediction framework for classifying throw types based on kinematic consistency; state-transition graph nodes represent different alignment configurations.
layer2.telemetry: Angular deviation \theta(t) = \cos^{-1}\left(\frac{{\bf r} \cdot {\bf v}}{|{\bf r}| |{\bf v}|}\right) serves as diagnostic metric.

primitives.name: Body-twist throw enhancement
primitives.verbatim_quote: They aid the throwing by a slight twist of the body.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'I_{\\text{body}}': 'Moment of inertia of torso about vertical axis [kg·m²]', '\\omega_{\\text{body}}': 'Angular velocity of body rotation [rad/s]'}
primitives.assumptions: Kinetic energy transfer from whole-body rotation to upper limb; conservation of angular momentum during the throw.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Maximum twist occurs at release point; excessive rotation leads to destabilization and reduced accuracy.

layer2.mapping: GSI anomaly detection for identifying inefficient energy transfer; GSE transition probabilities between pre-throw setup states.
layer2.telemetry: Measured rotational kinetic energy change compared to biomechanical models.

The forward-motion constraint enforces geometric optimality, ensuring maximal momentum transfer along the target direction. Body twist introduces rotational degrees of freedom, adding angular momentum that enhances overall throw velocity while maintaining alignment. These three primitives form a unified kinematic framework: practice improves baseline speed, geometric alignment preserves directional accuracy, and rotational assistance boosts magnitude. Their interplay creates a multi-dimensional state space for analyzing throwing performance. Failure occurs when any primitive breaks—loss of collinearity reduces accuracy, insufficient practice limits speed, and improper body rotation causes destabilization. This structure maps naturally to both GSI sequential testing (detecting deviations from optimal kinematics) and GSE state machines (modeling transitions between preparation, alignment, and execution phases).
